instructions: The night before, or at least 2 hours ahead, make the pickles. Stir 1/3 cup of the sugar and the 1 tbsp salt into 1 cup hot water until they dissolve, then add 1/2 cup rice vinegar. Peel 2 carrots and half the daikon, cut them into thin matchsticks and push them into the liquid. Cover and refrigerate.

At the same time, marinate the pork. Trim the tough outer layers off the lemongrass and finely mince the pale part, about 3 tbsp. Mince the shallot and 3 of the garlic cloves. Slice the 1.5 lb pork against the grain into thin slices about 1/4 inch thick. It's easier to slice if it's been in the freezer for 20 minutes.

In a big bowl, mix the lemongrass, shallot and garlic with the 1 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 1/2 tsp five spice, 1 tbsp bouillon powder, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp of the sugar and 2 tbsp of the oil. Add the pork and toss until every slice is coated. Cover and refrigerate.
On the day, bring a pot of water to a boil for the noodles.

Meanwhile, make the nuoc cham. Mince the last 2 garlic cloves. Stir the remaining 3 tbsp sugar into 1/3 cup warm water until it dissolves, then add the garlic, the remaining 3 tbsp fish sauce, the remaining 2 tbsp rice vinegar and the juice of the lime. Taste it. If it's too salty, add a splash of water. Thinly slice the 2 chilies and put them in a small bowl for the table.
Cook the 8 oz vermicelli for 3 to 5 minutes, or as the package says, until soft with no chalky center. Drain, rinse under cold water until cool and shake it as dry as you can.
Tear the lettuce into bite size pieces. Halve the cucumber lengthwise and slice it thin on an angle. Pick the mint leaves and roughly chop the 1/4 cup peanuts. Drain the pickles.

Heat a grill pan or large cast iron skillet over medium high with the last 1 tbsp oil. Lay in a single layer of pork, leaving room between the slices, and cook without moving them for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is dark brown and caramelized at the edges.

Flip the slices and cook the other side for 2 minutes. You're cooking it to 145°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest slice. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when there's no pink in the middle. Move them to a plate and cook the rest the same way. Watch for smoke, and turn the heat down a little if the marinade starts to burn.
Divide the noodles between 4 bowls. Pile the lettuce, cucumber, bean sprouts, pickles and mint around them and lay the pork on top. Scatter over the peanuts.
Serve with the nuoc cham to pour over and the sliced chilies on the side.
advance_prep_notes: Pickle the carrots and daikon and marinate the pork the night before, or at least 2 hours ahead.
method_notes: Both read versions marinate thin slices of pork in lemongrass, garlic, shallot, fish sauce and sugar, cook them hot until caramelized, and serve them over cold rinsed vermicelli with lettuce, cucumber, herbs, pickled carrot and daikon, peanuts and nuoc cham. Savory Sweet Spoon, the lead, adds oyster sauce, honey, five spice and bouillon powder to the marinade, marinates 30 minutes to overnight, and grills skewers or bakes them at 400°F. RecipeTin Eats marinates its lemongrass pork overnight, pickles the carrot and daikon for 2 hours, and serves the nuoc cham and lime on the side. This one cooks the slices in a grill pan without skewers and keeps the chilies at the table.
